summary: A diary entry on the evening of a public event says who was listening, what it was about and how the writer's day ended.
realLife: Mass Observation diarists wrote coronation day as an ordinary day: who listened to the broadcast, who did not, and what each person did instead.
sources: Sussex Library, Mass Observation 12 May 1937 and 2023 coronation-day diaries: https://blogs.sussex.ac.uk/librarycollections/2024/05/02/i-am-not-interested-in-the-coronation-similarities-and-dissimilarities-in-mass-observations-12th-may-diaries-from-1937-and-2023/
Diary of Samuel Pepys, April 1661 (coronation day, 23 April), Wikisource: https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Diary_of_Samuel_Pepys/1661/April
inGame: The first evening's diary entry (outline-diary moves watched, said, stance, mine, ahead); the household watchers are `we`, `us`, `watched-many` or `alone` from the address's own record.

turns.pulledBy: a household member's choice and the writer's own habits (traits: independent, shy)
turns.writesBack: the entry says where the writer was instead and what they heard about it later

turns.turn: The household is split on it.
turns.writesBack: the entry names the disagreement and who was on which side

turns.pulledBy: a late entry when the writer slept first (trait: meticulous, restless)
turns.writesBack: the entry says what the writer remembered, and less of it
